# Purpose and inputs

For an executable, function-by-function tutorial in Portuguese, see
`vignette("MettleRNASeq-passo-a-passo", package = "MettleRNASeq")`.
The complete English tutorial is available with
`vignette("MettleRNASeq-step-by-step", package = "MettleRNASeq")`.

MettleRNASeq provides an exploratory workflow for expression matrices with few
replicates: normalization, PCA-based gene selection, the original tailored
classification procedure, correlations and association rules. It starts from
gene expression matrices; read alignment and read counting occur upstream.

Most functions expect **samples in rows and genes in columns**, with numeric
values, unique sample names and unique gene names. `prepare_input_matrix()` also
accepts the transposed layout and identifies the sample axis using the metadata
labels. It returns one row per gene and condition, replicate columns, and a
`Condition` column. Classification requires the same genes in every condition
and equal replicate counts. At least two conditions and a split leaving both
training and test replicate columns are needed. Four replicates per condition
give the original three-training/one-test configuration at `train_percentage = .75`.

# Installation

Install the Bioconductor dependencies first, then the package and example engine:

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("BiocManager", "remotes", "randomForest"))
BiocManager::install(c("edgeR", "DESeq2"), ask = FALSE, update = FALSE)
remotes::install_github("SamellaSalles/MettleRNASeq")
```

This manual describes development version 1.0.0.9000. Until those changes are
released on GitHub, install the revised local checkout instead:

```{r local-install, eval=FALSE}
remotes::install_local("path/to/MettleRNASeq", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

The code declares R >= 4.2.0. This development version was tested on Windows
with R 4.4.1; use Bioconductor packages compatible with your R version.
`randomForest` runs the tutorial. Other caret engines may need their own packages
(for example, `ranger` or `e1071`). FP-growth additionally requires the optional
`fim4r` backend described in the arules documentation. Functions do not install
dependencies automatically. Use `packageVersion("MettleRNASeq")` to verify which
version is actually loaded.

# Included MSc data

The bone example contains eight samples and 235 genes from the author's MSc
analysis of FLASH versus STANDARD proton radiotherapy. The source study is
Velalopoulou et al. (2021), doi:10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-21-1500, GEO GSE173944.
These values were taken from the processed `B4.csv` matrix supplied with the
project and reshaped without numerical changes. They are already normalized and
the genes are already preselected. **Do not normalize this example again or feed
it into DESeq2 as raw counts.** It is a software demonstration, not the complete
transcriptome or a reproduction of all original results. Provenance and hashes
are in `inst/extdata/PROVENANCE.txt`.

```{r load-data}
library(MettleRNASeq)
expression <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "mestrado_bone_expression.csv",
  package = "MettleRNASeq"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
metadata <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "mestrado_bone_metadata.csv",
  package = "MettleRNASeq"))
stopifnot(identical(rownames(expression), metadata$Sample))
dim(expression)
table(metadata$Condition)
```

# Run the complete example

The installed script runs sample distances, PCA, feature selection,
classification, gene selection, ACC, ICC, correlation differences, rule mining
and rule comparison. It exports tables, an RDS results file, session information
and a PDF of plots. The MSc mode uses the processed matrix above; the synthetic
mode generates raw integer counts and also demonstrates TMM normalization.

```{r full-example, eval=FALSE}
source(system.file("examples", "run_example.R", package = "MettleRNASeq"))
result <- run_mettle_example("mestrado", output_dir = "example_mestrado")
raw_example <- run_mettle_example("synthetic", output_dir = "example_synthetic")
```

The short example uses three gene resamples and four replicate partitions.
It selects one resample with the highest recorded summary score to keep the
relationship outputs small. This selection is illustrative, not a significance
test or an estimate of biological discovery performance. In the tested Windows
environment, the MSc example selected 17 PCA genes and seven distinct genes
from the chosen resample; the two conditions produced six and four rules.
Results can vary across dependency versions or computational environments.
The demonstration is intentionally much smaller than the original analysis.

# Run individual stages

```{r individual-stages, eval=FALSE}
pca <- pca_analysis(expression, design_matrix = metadata, color_by = "Condition")
features <- feature_selection_pca(pca$pca_result, expression,
  num_pcs = 2, num_genes_per_pc = 12)
input <- prepare_input_matrix(features$selected_count_matrix,
  sample_vector = metadata$Sample, condition_vector = metadata$Condition)
classification <- classification_approach_advanced(input,
  algorithms = "rf", hyper_params = list(rf = data.frame(mtry = c(1, 3))),
  num_resamples = 3, num_genes = 10, seed = 123)
classification$partition_table
classification$status_table
classification$sample_map
selected <- genes_from_classification_results(classification$eval_table,
  classification$genes_table, features$selected_count_matrix,
  resamples = 1, return_plot = FALSE)
icc <- icc_analysis(selected$filtered_matrix, condition_split = c(4, 8))
differences <- icc_difference(icc)
```

`gene_ids_table` records sampled gene IDs, including repeated draws.
`genes_table` retains the legacy positions and carries ID metadata as an
attribute. Reordered gene columns are matched by ID in downstream selection.
If you save tables as CSV, also save `gene_ids_table` and pass it explicitly
when reconstructing the selection, because CSV does not retain R attributes.
Prefer `saveRDS()` when you want to preserve complete R objects.

# What the classification scores mean

The procedure samples genes and treats each gene-condition combination as a
row, with replicate expression values as predictors. This differs from a
conventional classifier whose rows are independent patients or biological
samples. Gene identity remains a predictor by default, as in the original
implementation. Internal caret training retains the original row indices for
training and internal evaluation; `train_accuracy` is not an independent
validation estimate.

For held-out replicate evaluation, that replicate's expression values are
repeated into the training-column layout. If more than one replicate is held
out, each is evaluated independently and their accuracies are averaged for the
partition. `summary_stat` then takes the median or mean over partitions within
each algorithm/resample. `test_eval_table` records the individual held-out
replicate scores. These are scores of this exploratory procedure and should not
be reported as validated prediction accuracy for unseen patients or unseen genes.

Failed fits stop with algorithm/resample/partition context by default.
`error_handling = "continue"` preserves failure records; an incomplete resample
has an `NA` summary. Inspect `status_table` before filtering by a cutoff.
When several algorithms are supplied, gene selection uses the union of eligible
resample IDs unless `algorithm` explicitly restricts the selection. Plots separate
algorithms and display the recorded summary statistic.

# Relationships and expression states

ICC correlates gene pairs within each condition. `icc_difference()` aligns both
matrix axes by gene ID before subtraction. It returns undirected pairs once
by default; `unique_pairs = FALSE` returns the legacy full table, including
self-pairs and both directions. ACC correlates each gene's expression vector
between conditions **by replicate position**, so that ordering must have a
meaningful interpretation; it does not create biological pairing automatically.
Small groups and constant expression vectors can give unstable or undefined
correlations.

Numeric expression passed to `mine_gene_associations()` is discretized by
arules. The default discretization is applied separately to each condition's
transactions. Therefore identically named bins need not have identical numerical
boundaries across conditions. Inspect the transaction item labels. To compare
expression states with a common meaning, supply factor columns constructed
using explicitly shared cut points or a documented biological definition.
The package preserves the original automatic behavior; it does not impose a
new discretization scheme.

`comparison = "genes"` compares complete LHS and RHS gene sets regardless of
their expression-state labels. `comparison = "items"` also compares those
labels. Neither comparison treats support, confidence or lift as rule identity.
Original rule tables are retained. Graphs project every antecedent gene to
every consequent gene; this is a visualization of an association rule, not proof
of direct regulation or causation. `maxlen = 2` in the tutorial restricts mining
to short rules; a maxlen warning reports that requested limit.

# Function reference

| Function | Role |
|:--|:--|
| `normalize_count_matrix` | Filter numeric counts and normalize with TMM, DESeq2 or non-centered scaling |
| `compute_distance_matrix` | Sample distances and optional heatmap |
| `pca_analysis` | PCA results and optional plots |
| `feature_selection_pca` | Select genes from absolute PCA loadings |
| `prepare_input_matrix` | Match metadata and create the gene-condition table |
| `classification_approach_advanced` | Gene resampling, replicate partitions and fit diagnostics |
| `genes_from_classification_results` | Select gene IDs and plot recorded scores |
| `acc_analysis` | Per-gene correlation across positional replicate vectors |
| `icc_analysis` | Gene-pair correlations within conditions |
| `icc_difference` | Aligned absolute correlation differences |
| `mine_gene_associations` | Rules and exact target-gene filtering |
| `compare_gene_rules` | Shared/unique complete gene sets or expression itemsets |

Use `help("classification_approach_advanced", package = "MettleRNASeq")` and
`browseVignettes("MettleRNASeq")` for installed documentation.

# Reproducibility and interpretation

Save the expression matrix, metadata, gene/sample mapping, random seed, tuning
grids, normalization settings, state definitions, results and `sessionInfo()`.
Do not compare runs with different gene universes or processing choices without
documenting those differences. The package complements statistical and
biological analysis; high exploratory scores or association rules do not
establish significance, causality or robustness to independent data.

Report bugs through the [issue tracker](https://github.com/SamellaSalles/MettleRNASeq/issues),
using a minimal example and session information. See `CONTRIBUTING.md` for
support and development practices. Cite the software repository/version and
the original method preprint, doi:10.1101/2025.05.06.652387, as appropriate.
